children: Japanese rubber futures rose on Tuesday, recouping some of the losses from the previous session, as a rally in Tokyo equities boosted investor sentiment.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for April delivery
was up 4.4 yen, or 1.05%, at 423.6 yen ($2.68) per kg
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 130 yuan, or 0.7%, to 18,800 yuan ($2,818.51) per metric ton
The most active December butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) fell 725 yuan, or 4.6%, to 15,020 yuan per metric ton
ended nearly 3% higher, extending its rebound from a tech-led selloff last week as AI-related stocks surged
Improved investor sentiment tends to support rubber futures
Sustained oversupply pressure is not yet visible, and prices are unlikely to keep falling, analysts from broker CITIC Securities Futures said in a note

The analysts said market expectations of El Niño's impact on rubber production may have been overestimated, potentially reducing concerns about supply tightness. They added that expectations of weaker overseas economies have accelerated the price decline since mid-October

Top consumer China's passenger vehicle exports jumped 68.2% year-on-year to 932,000 in October, while domestic sales fell 27.3% to 1.65 million, a 12th consecutive monthly decline, data from the China Passenger Car Association showed on Monday
Automobile sales could influence the intensity of automobile manufacturing, which involves using rubber-made tyres
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for February delivery (STFG7) last traded at 239.6 US cents per kg, up 1% as of 0700 GMT
